summary:
The Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act (P.L. 118-62) amends the USEC Privatization Act (42 U.S.C. 2297h-10a) to impose a new statutory prohibition on importing unirradiated low-enriched uranium (ULEU) from the Russian Federation. The Act adds subsection (d) to section 3112A, which, effective 90 days after enactment (August 11, 2024), bars importation of: (A) ULEU produced in the Russian Federation or by a Russian entity (defined as an entity organized under Russian law or otherwise subject to Russian jurisdiction); and (B) ULEU that the Secretary of Energy, Secretary of State, and Secretary of Commerce determine was exchanged, swapped, or otherwise obtained in lieu of such Russian-origin ULEU in a manner designed to circumvent the restriction. 

The Secretary of Energy, in consultation with the Secretaries of State and Commerce, is granted waiver authority. A waiver may be issued upon a determination that no alternative viable source of ULEU is available to sustain continued operation of a nuclear reactor or a U.S. nuclear energy company, or that importation is in the national interest. Any waiver is subject to annual quantitative caps on imports, including ULEU obtained under separative work unit contracts (whether or not derived from weapons-origin highly enriched uranium): 476,536 kilograms in calendar year 2024, 470,376 kg in 2025, 464,183 kg in 2026, and 459,083 kg in 2027. The Secretary of Commerce administers and enforces these limits in accordance with the existing Suspension Agreement and must impose a minimal burden on the commercial nuclear industry. A waiver terminates no later than January 1, 2028, and the Secretary of Energy must notify the Senate Committees on Energy and Natural Resources and on Finance, and the House Committees on Energy and Commerce and on Ways and Means upon issuance, identifying the recipient. The prohibition does not apply to imports by or under contract to the Department of Energy for national security or nonproliferation purposes, or to imports of non-uranium isotopes. Subsection (d) terminates on December 31, 2040.

Concurrently, the Act makes conforming amendments to section 3112A(c). These include: striking clauses (xi) through (xxvii) of paragraph (2)(A) (the pre-existing Russian ULEU import provisions), with that specific striking taking effect 90 days after enactment; striking paragraph (5) in its entirety; redesignating paragraphs (6) through (12) as (5) through (11); and updating multiple internal cross-references, including changing a termination date from December 31, 2040, to the effective date of the new prohibition. The remaining conforming amendments take effect upon enactment.
